parts.text: Figure 3.1 shows an electric shower. Figure 3.1 The temperature of water as it enters the shower is 15 °C. The water is heated in the shower. The water leaves the shower at a temperature of 38 °C.

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) The density of water is 1000 kg / m 3 . The specific heat capacity of water is 4200 J / (kg °C).

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) The water flows through the shower at a rate of 0.0045 m 3 / min. Show that the mass of water that leaves the shower in 4.0 min is 18 kg. [2]

ms.label: 3(a)(i)
ms.text:
(m =) ρV OR (m =) ρ × rate of flow × time
1000 × 0.0045 × 4(.0) (=18)

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate the energy required to increase the temperature of 18 kg of water from 15 °C to 38 °C. energy = ....................................................... J [2]

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) The energy in 3(a)(ii) is transferred to the water in 4.0 min. Calculate the power transferred to the water. power = ..................................................... W [2]

ms.label: 3(b)
ms.text:
any one from:
•
temperature of the water entering the shower is higher OR initial
temperature of water is higher
•
smaller mass / volume (flowing through the shower) per min
•
rate of flow of water decreases
